specificationNote: Registered so the route-to-family binding for this Kansas municipal route is a real, independently resolvable fact rather than a null agreeing with a null. It carries no legal statement that was not already approved, and it carries none this lane would have had to write: every section that would need one is declared unbound below.
whyThisExists: resolvePacketFamilyId in src/lib/rcap/render/commercial-admission.ts reads the registered specification, and the Grade-A admission compares the family the server believes a route delivers against the family a record proves. Without a registered specification this route resolved to no family at all, so the comparison could not be made.

copyRequirements.decisionRequired: How many copies the municipal court requires and what happens to each. Court by court, and not recorded.

feeAndWaiver.decisionRequired: The fee the convicting municipal court prescribes as costs under K.S.A. 12-4516(g)(2). Amounts vary by court and the memorandum records no statewide figure and no statutory waiver.

filingDestination.decisionRequired: Which municipal court clerk receives the filing, and whether that court publishes its own instrument or governs by charter ordinance. The memorandum yields to a published local form where one exists; Wichita proceeds under Charter Ordinance No. 224 §§ 12 and 13 and Topeka publishes its own petition and order.

hearingAndObjectionStops.decisionRequired: The situations in which a participant must stop and get help: the city prosecutor opposes, the municipal court sets a contested evidentiary hearing, or a factual ground is disputed.

postFilingTimeline.decisionRequired: The steps and timings after filing a packet may state as fact, including that on a grant the clerk sends a certified copy to the Kansas Bureau of Investigation.

serviceAndNotice.decisionRequired: That the court, not the participant, causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency under K.S.A. 12-4516(g)(1), stated in wording a packet may print.

statutoryAuthority.decisionRequired: The rule statement a packet may print for K.S.A. 12-4516, and which of the three-, five-, ten- and one-year branches a given participant's ordinance violation falls in. The branch turns on whether the ordinance violation would also have constituted a listed Kansas offence, which the approved memorandum records as the participant's own answer.

whyIncomplete: A packet may not be composed from this specification and no route may be proven on it while legalSectionsBound is false. Kansas municipal filing practice is court by court: the adopted memorandum yields to a municipal court's own published instrument where one exists, and the route contract holds a local_filing_configuration gate for exactly that reason. Until the per-court configuration is recorded, the destination, fee, copy count and hearing sections cannot be stated as fact.
